Profile

How the numbers work. Tier odds are the ones Valve disclosed in 2017: Mil-Spec 79.92%, Restricted 15.98%, Classified 3.20%, Covert 0.64%, Knife or Gloves 0.26%. Every item inside a tier is equally likely, 10% of eligible drops are StatTrak™, and wear follows the community-measured split of about 3 / 24 / 33 / 24 / 16% from Factory New to Battle-Scarred. There is no pity timer.

The shelf. All 42 CS2 weapon cases and 239 sticker and autograph capsules are here (281 total). The search bar looks through both families at once and also matches a case's rare-slot contents, so “gloves”, “knife”, “2024”, “paris” or a team name all find something. Crate icons, result art and inventory thumbnails come from Steam's item CDN; if an image cannot load, the page falls back to its own procedural texture.

Sticker capsules. Valve has never published capsule odds, so the Paper / Glitter / Holo / Foil / Gold split (78 / 17 / 4.1 / 0.8 / 0.1%) is a market model, not official data. A capsule that has no stickers in a tier has its remaining tiers renormalised so the opening always yields something. Capsules here cost $0.14–$3.67 and need no key.

Patterns and quality. Every weapon gets a deterministic 0–999 paint seed, an illustrative pattern grade (Blue Gem, Full fade, 4 webs, Fire & Ice, a Doppler phase shape and so on) and a float inside its wear bucket. Pattern grades are weighted so their average multiplier is close to 1.0. A special grade can add a premium, but it never changes the disclosed tier odds or the wear split.

Prices. Case, capsule, skin and sticker prices come from the CSGO Trader price feed snapshot for 29 Oct 2026, with a separate price for each wear and for StatTrak™. Missing wear points are interpolated from the nearest known prices, so a single drop can differ from the live market. Vanilla knives and gloves have no StatTrak in this model. A key costs $2.49.

Inventory and wiping. Every pull is added to the inventory, which keeps the latest 3,000 items and groups identical item, wear and StatTrak™ copies into one stack. The ledger above keeps all 5,000 most recent openings. “Wipe the books” resets the ledger, the drop history and the inventory together.

Not a bet. Nothing here uses real money or touches your Steam inventory. It is a simulation to show how the odds behave. Every case loses money on average, so treat real openings as entertainment spending. Case opening is restricted in some countries, for example Belgium.

Sources: Valve's odds and wear explainer · CSDB case odds · CSGO-API crate catalogue · CSGO Trader price feed · Steam Community Market. Not affiliated with Valve. Counter-Strike, CS2 and StatTrak are trademarks of Valve Corporation.
